- Register: "R049/2006-GB1-2010.01 Rev. 2"
- Document: "R49/2006/GB1-10.01"

The certificate document's own text says "OIML Certificate No R49/2006/GB1-10.01 Revision 2". The register says "R049/2006-GB1-2010.01 Rev. 2".

These appear to denote the same certificate. Let's break down:
- "R049" vs "R49" — this is the OIML recommendation R 49 (measuring systems for accuracy class 0.5... actually R49 is "Measuring systems for the fast dynamic measurement of loads" — water metering? No, R49 is "Measuring systems for the fast dynamic measurement of loads of vehicles" or similar). Anyway, "R049" vs "R49" is zero-padding drift — same recommendation.
- "2006" — the year of the recommendation edition, both agree.
- "GB1" — the issuing authority code (United Kingdom, GB1 = National Measurement Office), both agree.
- "2010.01" vs "10.01" — this is the certificate number; "10.01" is presumably short for "2010.01". So "2010.01" vs "10.01" is a truncation of the year prefix "20" — clearly denoting the same certificate number.
- "Rev. 2" vs "Revision 2" — same revision.

So these are number format differences that clearly denote the same certificate. Per the rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

So verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's value "R049/2006-GB1-2010.01 Rev. 2".

One short sentence: "R49 vs R049 is zero-padding and 10.01 vs 2010.01 is year truncation; both denote the same certificate, so keep the register's canonical form."
